dedupe_keys.name: impact of reflective roadways on simulated heat strain at the tokyo paris and los angeles olympics

description: Impact of Reflective Roadways on Simulated Heat Strain at the Tokyo, Paris, and Los Angeles Olympics is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Jennifer Vanos, Arizona State University (asu.edu). This study models the progression of heat strain in elite marathon and race walk athletes competing on traditional dark asphalt, reflective pavement, or shaded asphalt in past and future Olympic Games (Tokyo (Sapporo), Paris, Los Angeles). Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 15 top-level files. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-azgv-b757. Keywords: Heat, Reflective Pavement, Olympics, Heat Strain, Core Temperature. Published 2025-06-12. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
